objective: Port netty-codec-http3 4.2.19.Final (io.netty.handler.codec.http3) to Netty.NET.Handler.Codec.Http3 with the original names, structure, comments and tests. The QUIC-free closure was ported first; the 56 main units that need codec-classes-quic (io.netty.handler.codec.quic) followed on its API layer (Netty.NET.Handler.Codec.Quic, stage 1) on 2026-11-27. The test sources that need EmbeddedQuicChannel/EmbeddedQuicStreamChannel or a stage-2 unit are recorded as deferred-to-module.

ownerDecisions: Project, folder and assembly names are the namespace root of the module (owner decision 2026-11-19, see docs/codec-base-porting.md): each codec module takes the namespace of its main package, and the tests use <project>.Tests like the other test projects.

2026-11-27: codec-http3 is Netty.NET.Handler.Codec.Http3 (one project per Maven module, the 2026-11-19 rule; no new name choice); it references Netty.NET.Handler.Codec.Http, and its tests are Netty.NET.Handler.Codec.Http3.Tests. The example package io.netty.handler.codec.http3.example (test sources) is deferred with the rest of the QUIC-bound units.

2026-11-27 (main port): Netty.NET.Handler.Codec.Http3 also references Netty.NET.Handler.Codec.Quic, the codec-classes-quic API layer, whose InternalsVisibleTo opens its internals to this assembly and its tests; inside Netty.NET.Handler.Codec.* the simple name Quic is that namespace.

statusMeaning.verified: Every declared original test is mapped to a C# test with the same name (case may differ) and passes.
statusMeaning.clr-adapted: Ported with the original names, structure and comments; every CLR difference is stated in a // CLR: comment and in this entry.
statusMeaning.jvm-only-replaced: JVM-only metadata or documentation unit replaced by its recorded CLR counterpart.
statusMeaning.deferred-to-module: 2026-11-26 checker rule: the unit needs a Netty module that has no C# project yet (here codec-classes-quic): it imports that module's package (blockingImports, recomputed from the source) or names a deferred type of this module (via). It is ported with that module; this is not a decision against porting it. Its declared tests and the count of its original comments are recorded.

The Java byte value & 0xFF and the System.Byte value are the same index; data.charAt(i) & 0xFF keeps the low eight bits of the char as Java does. The codes (below 2^30) and the EOS padding bits are non-negative, so OR-ing them into the long as uint (zero extension, which avoids the C# sign-extension warning CS0675) gives the value of Java's int to long widening.

Test helper: internal sealed EmbeddedQuicChannel : EmbeddedChannel, IQuicChannel, as the Java class extends EmbeddedChannel and implements QuicChannel. createStream(type, handler, promise) is CreateStreamAsync returning a completed Task<IQuicStreamChannel> with a new EmbeddedQuicStreamChannel whose id comes from the per-channel generator (server 1, client 0, step 2; AtomicLong is a StrongBox<long> attribute updated with Interlocked.Add, because AttributeKey<T> needs a reference type); close(applicationClose, error, reason, promise) is CloseAsync(bool, int, ByteBuf, CancellationToken), which records the error code and releases the reason once (a continuation of the close Task on the first close, at once afterwards); collectStats/collectPathStats return a faulted Task with NotSupportedException. localAddress()/remoteAddress() override LocalAddress/RemoteAddress (null); flush()/read() only narrow return types, so they are inherited; config() is NewConfig() returning the delegating EmbeddedQuicChannelConfig (IQuicChannelConfig, every IChannelConfig member delegated, the deprecated max-messages members [Obsolete]). prependChannelConsumer keeps its anonymous handler as the nested ChannelConsumerHandler. EnumMap is a Dictionary, ConcurrentLinkedQueue a ConcurrentQueue<int> returned as an IReadOnlyCollection<int> for unmodifiableCollection. Exercised by every connection, control-stream, QPACK and unidirectional-stream test of this port; a temporary scratch test (not committed) also checked the stream ids (server 1, 3; client 0), the reason releases and the recorded error codes on 2026-11-27.

Test helper: internal sealed EmbeddedQuicStreamChannel : EmbeddedChannel, IQuicStreamChannel. The constructors keep the Java signatures (parent, localCreated, type, id, handlers) over EmbeddedChannel(parent, DefaultChannelId.NewInstance(), true, false, ...); the id, type and localCreated attributes are AttributeKey<object> holding boxed values. shutdown/shutdownInput/shutdownOutput(int, promise) are ShutdownAsync/ShutdownInputAsync/ShutdownOutputAsync(int) returning a completed Task and recording the first error code (int?), the no-argument forms are IDuplexChannel members, and writeInboundWithFin/writeInboundFin call the interface default ShutdownInputAsync() (error 0) and fire ChannelInputShutdownEvent and ChannelInputShutdownReadComplete. The wrapping Unsafe of unsafe() is one override of WriteTransportAsync, because Channel.Unsafe is folded into AbstractChannel: a QuicStreamFrame with FIN marks the output shut down (error 0) when the write Task completes. updatePriority returns a faulted Task (NotSupportedException); config() is NewConfig() returning the delegating EmbeddedQuicStreamChannelConfig (readFrames false, its own allowHalfClosure; the delegating calls of the [Obsolete] max-messages members compile under a CS0612 suppression). A temporary scratch test (not committed) checked the FIN write, writeInboundWithFin, the default id, type and localCreated values and the config type on 2026-11-27.

Cause: Http3FrameToHttpObjectCodec maps PromiseCombiner to Task.WhenAll(combiner) + Http3CodecUtils.Cascade; the Transport's write Tasks run their continuations asynchronously (ChannelOutboundBuffer.WritePromise, RunContinuationsAsynchronously), so the Task.WhenAll of a message written as two or more frames completes later on a thread-pool thread, and the combined promise and its SHUTDOWN_OUTPUT listener run after writeOutbound returns, while Java's PromiseCombiner completes them on the event loop when the last write completes. Single-frame writes (Http3CodecUtils.Write, whose continuation uses EventExecutorTaskScheduler) and testEncodeCombination (whose test handler's promises complete synchronously) pass.

notApplicableMethods.sourceContract: Iterable.spliterator() of a settings object holding two entries is non-null and its estimateSize() is greater than zero.
notApplicableMethods.reason: java.util.Spliterator is the JVM's traversal and partitioning source of java.util.stream, reached through the default method Iterable.spliterator(); Http3Settings implements IEnumerable<KeyValuePair<long, long>> (Http3Settings entry), and the CLR enumerable has no spliterator or size estimate. The enumeration of the entries is covered by testIteratorProvidesEntries and testForEachConsumer, which are ported and pass.

notApplicableMethods.sourceContract: put(1, null) (HTTP3_SETTINGS_QPACK_MAX_TABLE_CAPACITY with a null Long) throws NullPointerException from checkNotNull(value, "value") in verifyStandardSetting.
notApplicableMethods.reason: Http3Settings.Put takes the value as a long, because a Long parameter is a CLR long (Http3Settings.cs: "A Long parameter is a long, so the checkNotNull(value) of a standard setting has no counterpart"); a null value cannot be passed (CS0037, null is not convertible to the non-nullable value type long), so the null check the method tests does not exist.

The h3spec server program in namespace Netty.NET.Handler.Codec.Http3 (its package), placed in the examples executable test/Netty.NET.Handler.Codec.Http3.Examples because it is a main program, not a test. NioDatagramChannel.class is Channel<QuicEndpointChannel>(): msquic owns the UDP socket, so the codec runs on the CLR-only QuicEndpointChannel that takes the datagram channel's place (owner decision 2026-11-27, docs/codec-classes-quic-porting.md, Stage 2). main(String...) is a public static async Task Main(string[]) that the CLR-only ExampleLauncher of the examples executable (StartupObject, copied from src/Netty.NET.Example/ExampleLauncher.cs) runs by its Java class name; sync()/get()/getNow() are awaits and shutdownGracefully() is ShutdownGracefullyAsync() with the Task discarded. MultiThreadIoEventLoopGroup and NioIoHandler are the Transport's. maxIdleTimeout(5000, MILLISECONDS) takes a TimeSpan. A Java String passed as a CharSequence is a StringCharSequence. QuicStreamChannel.SHUTDOWN_OUTPUT has no counterpart in codec-quic (IQuicStreamChannel), so the write Task is continued with ShutdownOutputAsync(). The anonymous Http3RequestStreamInboundHandler is a private nested class and CharsetUtil.US_ASCII is Encoding.ASCII. The anonymous ChannelInitializer<QuicChannel>/<QuicStreamChannel> are ActionChannelInitializers whose delegates are initChannel (the original comments stay in them). new InetSocketAddress(port) is the wildcard IPEndPoint(IPAddress.Any, port) (Transport convention). SelfSignedCertificate is @Deprecated and not ported (handler, deprecated-not-ported): the key and certificate are a self-signed bundle of the PkiTesting port (CertificateBuilder cn=localhost, ECDSA P-256, as Netty.NET.Example's ServerUtil), passed as forServer(cert.key(), null, cert.cert()) through X509Bundle.GetKeyPair()/GetCertificate(). Integer.parseInt is int.Parse with an optional sign and the invariant culture. channel.eventLoop().submit(runnable) is the SubmitAsync(Action) extension of the event loop with the Task discarded, and System.out.println is Console.WriteLine; Http3ServerConnectionHandler(handler, null, null, null, true) is the same five-argument constructor. Run on loopback on 2026-11-27 (Windows 11 10.0.26300, .NET 10.0.11, Debug): "Http3SpecTestServer 19002" printed H3SPEC_SERVER_READY on stdout; "example.Http3ClientExample -Dport=19002" printed "Hello World!\r\n" and exited 0, and an HTTP/3 HttpClient GET and POST got status 404, version 3.0, server: netty and body "Hello World!\r\n". h3spec itself (a Haskell tool) was not run: it is not installed and downloads were out of scope.

NioDatagramChannel.class is Channel<QuicEndpointChannel>(): msquic owns the UDP socket, so the codec runs on the CLR-only QuicEndpointChannel that takes the datagram channel's place (owner decision 2026-11-27, docs/codec-classes-quic-porting.md, Stage 2). main(String...) is a public static async Task Main(string[]) that the CLR-only ExampleLauncher of the examples executable (StartupObject, copied from src/Netty.NET.Example/ExampleLauncher.cs) runs by its Java class name; sync()/get()/getNow() are awaits and shutdownGracefully() is ShutdownGracefullyAsync() with the Task discarded. MultiThreadIoEventLoopGroup and NioIoHandler are the Transport's. maxIdleTimeout(5000, MILLISECONDS) takes a TimeSpan. A Java String passed as a CharSequence is a StringCharSequence. QuicStreamChannel.SHUTDOWN_OUTPUT has no counterpart in codec-quic (IQuicStreamChannel), so the write Task is continued with ShutdownOutputAsync(). The anonymous Http3RequestStreamInboundHandler is a private nested class and CharsetUtil.US_ASCII is Encoding.ASCII. Binding the endpoint with the client codec (bind(0) is BindAsync(0), the wildcard address) records the local address, and QuicChannel.newBootstrap(channel) is IQuicChannel.NewBootstrap(channel), whose ConnectAsync runs QuicConnection.ConnectAsync through the endpoint. InsecureTrustManagerFactory.INSTANCE is the handler port's accepting RemoteCertificateValidationCallback; Http3.newRequestStream is Http3.NewRequestStreamAsync; NetUtil.LOCALHOST4.getHostAddress() is the IPAddress text and the port prints with the invariant culture; System.err.print is Console.Error.Write and content() the Content property. Http3ServerExample.PORT is 9999 unless the CLR-only -Dport=<port> launcher property gives another one. Run on loopback on 2026-11-27 (Windows 11 10.0.26300, .NET 10.0.11, Debug): against "example.Http3ServerExample 19000" (3 runs) and "Http3SpecTestServer 19002" (1 run) with -Dport: stderr was exactly "Hello World!\r\n" (the 14-byte DATA frame), stdout empty, exit code 0, about 2.3 s per run (the stream closed after the FIN, then the QuicChannel and the endpoint closed).
